ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, in triangle ABC, AB is the vertical side, BC is the horizontal side, and AC is the hypotenuse from A to C; at B there is a right angle. The three sides AB, BC, and AC respectively serve as the diameters of three semicircles: the semicircle on AB is on the left side, the semicircle on BC is below, and the semicircle on AC is above. Then reason: The area of the semicircle on AB is 8π. The formula for the area of a semicircle is (1/2)πr^2, so (1/2)πr^2 = 8π, giving r^2 = 16, r = 4. Therefore AB is the diameter of this semicircle, AB = 8. The arc length of the semicircle on AC is 8.5π. The arc length of a semicircle is πr, so the radius of the semicircle on AC is 8.5, and the diameter AC = 17. Because ∠ABC is a right angle, AC is the hypotenuse, use the Pythagorean theorem: BC = sqrt(17^2 - 8^2) = sqrt(289 - 64) = sqrt(225) = 15. The radius of the semicircle on BC is half of the diameter BC, so the radius is 15/2 = 7.5.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: triangle ABC has AB vertical, BC horizontal, and AC slanted, so the right angle is at B; the semicircles are drawn with diameters AB, BC, and AC. From the text, the semicircle on AB has area 8π, so use (1/2)πr^2 = 8π to get r = 4 and hence AB = 8. Also from the text, the arc length of the semicircle on AC is 8.5π; since a semicircle arc has length πr, the radius on AC is 8.5, so AC = 17. Because AC is the hypotenuse of the right triangle shown, apply the Pythagorean theorem: BC = sqrt(17^2 - 8^2) = sqrt(289 - 64) = 15. The radius of the semicircle on BC is half its diameter, so the answer is 15/2 = 7.5.
